CAV ORDER  1.

The applicant has preferred the second bail application under Section 439 of CrPC for grant of regular bail as he is in jail since 06.09.2022 in connection with Crime No.281/2019 registered at Police Station- Balod, District- Balod (C.G.) for the offence punishable under Section 420/34 of IPC and Sections 3, 4 & 5 of Enami Chit Aur Dhan Parichalan Adhiniyam and Section 10 of C. G. ke Nikshepo Ke Hito Ka Sanrakshan Adhiniyam, 2005.

sentences.text:
His first bail application was dismissed on merits passed in MCRC No.11232 of 2022 dated 06.02.2023.
2.

The case of prosecution in brief, is that the complainant Vivek Kumar Hirwani lodged a report that the present applicant who was working as Managing Director of Indusware Industries Limited and Indus Broker House Pvt. Ltd. allured him to deposit money in the company with an assurance that the money would be doubled within a short span of time with a high degree of interest and the same was not returned back and all of a sudden the company was closed after collection of money.

It is alleged that said circulation of money was made without any sanction of the RBI or SEBI, and thus the offence alleged has been committed.
3. Counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent person and has been falsely implicated in this case.
He further submits that though the first bail application was dismissed on merits however, liberty was reserved to renew the prayer within four months if trial is not concluded.

He submits that till date charges have not been framed and no substantial progress has Arunesh Sita vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10401888/
1 taken place, therefore, the applicant may be released on bail.
4.

entities.text: Arunesh Sita vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, State counsel opposes the bail application and submits that by a detailed order the first application of applicant was dismissed on merits.

He further submits that as per prosecution, the accused in this case received huge amount of money from various investors, did not pay back the amount and after closing the company ran away and thereby committed the said offence.
He submits that the applicant is resident of Bihar there is all possibility of his absconding from trial.

Looking to the evidence collected by the prosecution and various people have been cheated by the accused persons and the name of the present applicant is also reflected in the statement of victims, therefore, his bail application may be rejected.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and considered their rival submissions and also perused the case diary.

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, considering that the bail application was dismissed on merits though liberty was reserved to renew the prayer within four months if trial is not concluded, at this stage looking to the evidence collected by the prosecution and the statement of victims, I am not inclined to allow this bail application.
7. Accordingly, the second bail application is rejected.
8. However, it is expected that trial Court will expedite the trial.

Sd/-
(Sachin Singh Rajput) Judge parul Arunesh Sita vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10401888/
